**Summary of findings:**
- Test image shows a field-wide view of tomato plants that are low and prostrate/sprawling across rows, with green foliage and red-brown soil. No close-up symptoms visible.
- **Strongest match: Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus** — Both CMV reference images (Bugwood_1568047, 1568048) show virtually identical field-wide views with the same layout, overcast sky, soil type, and plant appearance. The test image is Bugwood_1568052 — only 4 numbers away, indicating the same photographer/collection/disease session.
- CMV symptom description confirms: plants appear "bushy and stunted" with low, sprawling growth — consistent with what the test image shows.
- All other wilt candidates (Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Bacterial_Canker) showed single-plant close-ups with drooping or browning, which differ from the uniform field-wide low-sprawling pattern in the test image.
- Fungal/leaf diseases (Early_Blight, Septoria, Gray_Mold, Powdery_Mildew, etc.) are leaf-level diseases clearly not matching this field-level whole-plant view.
